title: OEE Framework
body: ADW's trucks and excavators sit at 90%+ mechanical availability, yet tonnage still comes up short — because the losses aren't in the machines, they're in Performance (standby, waiting for excavator, no location) and Quality (wrong-tip events, crusher bin starvation). If you only watch availability, you'll think the fleet is fine while output keeps bleeding out through dispatch and sequencing gaps.
keyPoints: Availability tells you the machine is capable of running, not that it's producing — don't let a strong A&U number talk you out of chasing standby time.
Dump truck utilization runs 15-25 points below availability at ADW. That gap is the Performance loss, and it's driven by dispatch sequencing and face availability, not mechanical condition.
Quality in load-and-haul means the load went to the right place at the right spec — wrong-tip NCRs and crusher bin-choke stoppages are quality failures even though the truck completed a cycle.
The three factors compound multiplicatively (OEE = A × P × Q ÷ 10,000), so a strong Availability number can still mask a weak overall result if Performance and Quality are dragging.
This lines up with the Kaizen finding: people and process, not equipment, are the primary constraint on output here.
apply: When you're at the loading face or ROM pad, don't just check if machines are running — watch for standby causes (waiting on excavator, no location) and confirm trucks are tipping to the correct blend location, since those are the two loss categories actually costing tonnes.
